name: Lungo
caffeine: The same dose as an espresso, but more water through the puck pulls out a little more total caffeine.

house.ask: Not printed on the menus: ask at lineup whether there is an espresso machine, whether the bar will pull a lungo on request, and the price.

what: A lungo is an espresso run long: the same 18 to 20 g dose pushed out to 50 to 72 g, about 1:3 to 1:4. Every drop goes through the bed under pressure, so it is thinner and more extracted. The name is Italian for long; it is not an americano.
taste: Thinner and longer than espresso, more bitter, with a drying, papery finish and the bean's darker notes pulled over its fruit.

steps: Dose 18 to 20 g into a warm double basket, ground a little coarser.
Tamp level, lock in and pull onto a scale.
Stop at 50 to 60 g, or as far as about 72 g.
Set the yield by tasting the far end: stop before the cup turns hollow and drying.
make.ratio: About 1:3 to 1:4, against 1:2 for a normale
make.cup: Warmed 3 oz demitasse, filled higher than an espresso

serve: On a saucer with a spoon, in a warmed cup at the 3 oz end of the range. It goes out alone; there is enough liquid that no water back is expected.
story: Lungo is Italian for long, and many guests know it from capsule machines, where a button is marked lungo. It suits the guest who wants espresso to last past two sips but will not take an americano.
guest: A lungo is an espresso pulled long: a few more sips, but more bitter. If you would like it milder, an americano is gentler.
watch: A guest wanting milder goes to the americano, never the lungo: more water through the puck means more bitterness.
Thinner per sip is not less coffee: it carries a little more caffeine than an espresso.
Some bars call a watered shot a lungo; confirm what the house means.

recall.prompt: How is a lungo made, and how does it differ from an americano?
recall.answer: The same 18 to 20 g dose pushed to 50 to 72 g, every drop under pressure; an americano adds water after. Thin, bitter, drying, in a warmed demitasse.

quiz.q: A guest wants an espresso that is milder and longer. What do you suggest?
quiz.explain: Water added after the shot dilutes without pulling bitterness; a lungo forces more water through the puck, so it reads harsher.

quiz.q: From 18 g of coffee, about how much does a lungo yield?
quiz.explain: A lungo runs 1:3 to 1:4. About 36 g is a normale, 18 to 27 g a ristretto.

quiz.q: From the same dose, how does a lungo's total caffeine compare with an espresso's?
quiz.explain: More water through the same puck extracts further, caffeine included. Thinner per sip is not less coffee.

video.watchFor: How the shot runs on past a normal espresso into a longer cup, and where it is stopped. Any good lungo stops before the stream turns pale and the cup turns hollow and bitter.
